title: Approximate selective state indexing under one-bit query noise
question: Can an approximate Hamming index preserve learned persistent-state retrieval while reducing the number of state items seen by the learned scorer?
hypothesis: H_index: an approximate radius-2 state index can retain the target state for noisy queries often enough that the same trained scorer preserves capability while reducing scorer work from O(M) to O(K) with K <= 4.

arms.name: analytic
arms.intervention: identity state encoder evaluated by full scan and indexed shortlist

arms.name: learned_full
arms.intervention: trained bilinear state addressor over all M state items

arms.name: learned_indexed
arms.intervention: the same trained addressor over the Hamming-index shortlist

arms.name: no_learning
arms.intervention: fresh frozen random addressor over all M state items

endpoints.name: index_target_recall
endpoints.role: secondary — whether the approximate index retains the true state item

endpoints.name: full_route_macs
endpoints.role: audit — learned scorer work over M

endpoints.name: indexed_route_macs
endpoints.role: audit — learned scorer work over K

endpoints.name: index_build_reads
endpoints.role: audit — one-time state reads for index construction

decision_rule.condition: learned_indexed_top1 remains within 0.05 absolute of learned_full_top1 and index_target_recall is at least 0.95 while mean shortlist is strictly below M
decision_rule.licenses: bounded support for an approximate selective state-index intervention under the registered noisy task
decision_rule.does_not_license: sublinear end-to-end computation, learned indexing, or general memory retrieval

decision_rule.condition: the indexed arm loses more than 0.05 absolute capability or index_target_recall falls below 0.95
decision_rule.licenses: the registered approximate index does not preserve sufficient capability under this task

held_constant: state bits = 10 and fixed Hamming-3 codebook of 64 codes
each query differs from its target state code by exactly one bit
same trained addressor weights are used for learned_full and learned_indexed
Hamming radius = 2 and shortlist K = 4 are fixed before the run
state pool is fixed during each 256-query evaluation block and index is built once
opaque state addresses never appear in queries
no target address or gold field enters the index
C5 and all earlier REP evidence remain frozen
